subject: Conference entry queue causing lead loss / consent sync plan
messages:
From: SummitWorks Events <events@summitworks.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:23:00 +0000
Subject: Badge scanners slowing at entry — missing opt-ins and duplicates

Hi Soojin,

Quick heads up from site ops — our entry lane badge scanners started lagging around 10:10am local yesterday. When the scanner goes into a slow state it sometimes drops the consent checkbox and writes a duplicate record with a slightly different timestamp, which makes the HubSpot sync create dupe contacts and lose the opt-in flag.

Attached is an excerpt of the scanner log (scanner-log-20261104.csv) showing the repeated badge reads and the timestamp drift. We're worried this will inflate counts and, more importantly, we may be missing lawful opt-ins for follow-ups.

Can your team advise an immediate mitigation we can do today for the remainder of the show (besides restarting devices)? Also curious what fields we should be mapping so we can reconcile duplicates and restore opt-in status during a post-event backfill.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Liam
Event Ops, SummitWorks

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Liam Porter <liam@sw-events.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Badge scanners slowing at entry — missing opt-ins and duplicates

Thanks Liam — looping Ben and Marissa. High-level plan:

1) Short-term (on-site today): enable offline cache + batch upload flow and a temporary dedupe key based on badge_id + event_id so duplicates with timestamp drift don't create new records.
2) Mid-term (post-event Recon): use scanner logs + badge read sequence to reconcile duplicate records, and if any record is missing the opt-in flag but has a timestamp within the same session window, we set opt-in = true if the consent snippet was captured elsewhere (QR/waiver).
3) CRM mapping: we need a canonical consent source field (consent_channel) and a boolean (marketing_opt_in) in HubSpot and Salesforce. Vanessa, can you confirm mapping and whether we can run a partial import that preserves contact IDs?

Ben — can you take point on the cache + dedupe key? Marissa — please confirm on-site fallback (paper waiver / QR) and whether the team can mark attendees for a quick re-scan. I'll coordinate comms with SummitWorks.

Soojin
Director, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam Porter <liam@sw-events.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Badge scanners slowing at entry — missing opt-ins and duplicates

Quick technical notes after I parsed the CSV:

- The scanners emit a badge_id, read_sequence, and device_local_ts. The duplicates are the same badge_id with read_sequence incrementing but the backend is ingesting them as new because the data pipeline currently uses only the device_local_ts as a near-unique key.
- Short fix: apply dedupe by badge_id + event_id + floor(read_sequence/5) (i.e., group bursts from the same attendee into a single record). That will collapse duplicates caused by retried reads without losing legitimate separate check-ins for multi-event passes.
- For missing opt-in: I can add a small boolean flag in the ingest layer that prefers a consent value if it exists anywhere in the session bucket; otherwise mark consent_source = 'scanner-missing' so we can find these during backfill.

I'll push a quick config change to enable the session-bucket dedupe and the consent preference today; should be a 30–45 minute rollout with a short restart window (5 mins).

Attaching a consent snippet we discussed (consent-snippet-v2.docx) with suggested wording for QR fallback and waiver scan.

—Ben
Senior Field Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Liam Porter <liam@sw-events.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 19:02:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Badge scanners slowing at entry — missing opt-ins and duplicates

On-site update: team confirmed two practical fallbacks we can run in parallel for the afternoon sessions:

- QR consent fallback: stations at information desk where attendees can scan and confirm opt-in. We'll print a short QR card with the short consent text from the docx attachment and a tiny QR landing page.
- Batch upload: we'll keep a CSV of resolved duplicates and flagged records and perform hourly batch uploads into a staging contact list in HubSpot. Vanessa — we'll need a safe staging list that doesn't trigger automations.

We can also have volunteers with tablets re-scan a subset of attendees in the most affected lane to expedite reconciliation. Estimated manual re-scan rate: ~120/hr per volunteer.

Marissa
Field Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — CRM notes and constraints:

- HubSpot: We'll create a temporary 'SummitWorks - Nov 2026 (staging)' static list and disable all enrollment/automation triggers. For imports, please include our canonical contact_id (if available), email, badge_id, event_id, marketing_opt_in (true/false), consent_channel, source_note. If there's no contact_id, HubSpot will create a new contact; dedupe will be applied where email + badge_id match.
- Salesforce: we can do an upsert on External_Id__c = badge_id + "-SW2026" so duplicates collapse. We will set the Consent_Channel__c and Marketing_Opt_In__c fields as mapped.
- For reconciliation: share the scanner-log CSV + our session-bucket output and I will run a staged merge in the CRM with pre-merge backups.

Linking a Drive sheet for the import mapping and the SOW/DocuSign we discussed: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSummitWorksOps
